Shaped rows, split pack and the Parquet pool

Races the new memory-compression build against the old one, then packs a Parquet file over as many helpers as this device can carry. Measure only; nothing is sent anywhere.

Parquet file (optional)

Choose any Parquet file to add the split pack and pool tests, for example the NYC taxi file yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet (about 48 MB) or sba-1group.parquet from the project folder. The file is only read, never uploaded. Without a file only the shaped rows race runs.

What is measured

1. Shaped rows: memory-compression's old build (2.17.6 with the hex and light-trial changes) against the new build with shaped rows, packing and unpacking 20,000 sparse records in a fresh frame for every sample, in alternating order (9 pairs per case in the Quick run, 31 in the Full run). 2. Split pack: one row group of your file is decoded once, then packed as K row ranges over K helpers; K goes 1, 2, 4 ... up to the plan above, never more (2 runs each in Quick, 3 in Full). 3. Parquet pool: every column chunk is decoded on any free helper and packed per row range, with the ranges cut on the page or inside the helpers, in turn; the layouts use at most the plan's helpers (2 layouts and 2 runs each in Quick, 3 layouts and 4 runs each in Full). Stop waits for the step under way, then keeps everything so far. If the browser closes during a run, reopening this page in the same tab says which step it was on.
